steps: Look at the bottom-right corner of the screen, next to the clock.
If you cannot see the Earshot icon, click the small ^ arrow to show hidden icons.
Click the Earshot icon once with the left mouse button. Do not double-click.
A small card should appear near the clock.
Right-click the Earshot icon near the clock.
A menu opens above it.
Click Start.
Click Power.
Click Shut down. Do not click Restart.
Wait for this computer to turn off, then press the power button to turn it back on.
Sign in, then open this window again.
Click Start.
Click Power.
Click Sleep.
Wait at least thirty seconds, then wake this computer up.
Sign in, then open this window again.
Click Start.
Click Power.
Click Restart.
When it has signed you back in, open this window again.
Click Start.
Click Settings.
Click Bluetooth and devices.
Find your AirPods in the list.
Click Connect.
Put the AirPods in your ears.
Play something on your phone, such as music or a video.
Windows shows a box asking "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?"
Click Yes to allow it, or No to refuse.
Right-click the Start button.
Click Task Manager.
Click Startup apps on the left.
Find Earshot in the list.
Press the Ctrl, Shift and Esc keys together. Task Manager opens.
Find Earshot in the list. If you cannot see it, click the small arrow next to Apps or Background processes to open the list.
Click Earshot once.
Click End task at the top of the window.
The Earshot icon near the clock goes away. Leave the AirPods connected and playing.
Right-click an empty part of the desktop.
Click Display settings.
Find Scale, set it to 150%, then set it back to what it was.
Right-click an empty part of the desktop.
Click Personalise.
Click Colours.
Change "Choose your mode" between Light and Dark.

entries.plain: Compare the card with what your iPhone shows. Does every battery number on the card agree with the iPhone, give or take one step of 10, with nothing shown for a part the card has no number for? If the card shows no battery number at all, answer "not sure".

entries.plain: Close the case lid with the AirPods inside, and leave the card open for a minute.

entries.plain: A minute later, is every battery number on the card greyed, with how long ago it was read beside it? The numbers stay whether or not closing the lid disconnected the AirPods. None may look current.

entries.plain: Disconnect the AirPods from this computer again: left-click the Earshot icon, or the gauge if you have one, then click Disconnect on the card.

entries.plain: With the AirPods not connected to this computer, does the card say "Not seen yet" rather than guessing whether they are on your phone or in their case?

entries.plain: Within about ten seconds, did a small card with the left, right and case figures appear by itself, on the screen the gauge is on, while the window you were typing in kept the keyboard focus?

entries.scriptText: preconditions

entries.scriptText: to-pc-no-timeout
entries.plain: No switch to this computer should have run out of time.

entries.plain: You should have heard this computer's sound in the AirPods after every switch to this computer, and this test should have seen them connected.

entries.scriptText: to-pc-acceptable

entries.plain: Is there a ring round the earbud picture on the gauge? (It appears once an earbud has a reading, of any age, so no ring is a fine answer when no earbud has been heard yet.)

entries.plain: Open Windows Settings, click Personalisation, click Colours, choose a different accent colour, then look at the gauge. Choose your usual accent colour again afterwards.

entries.plain: Does the gauge show the case mark with a grey ring and number, and does the card show the case figure with the "about" sign (two wavy lines) before it and how long ago the reading was? If no figure has that sign, answer "not sure": Earshot estimates only once it has learned a charge rate from your own AirPods.
